algorithm_long: DFT-Stack: a cross-fitted, simplex-weighted stack of composition experts for the four Matbench v0.1 composition tasks, using Materials Project DFT data as transfer-learning input features. EXTERNAL DATA DISCLOSURE: besides the formula-derived descriptors, the experts receive a block of Materials Project PBE DFT features taken from matminer's matbench_mp_gap (PBE band gap) and matbench_mp_e_form (PBE formation energy) datasets, matched to each task composition by reduced formula (most stable polymorph by formation energy, plus polymorph aggregates; unmatched compositions get missing values and a dft_matched = 0 indicator). These DFT values are STRUCTURE-DERIVED: every Materials Project entry is a DFT calculation on a crystal structure, and per reduced formula we take the entry (polymorph) with the lowest formation energy per atom plus aggregates over all polymorphs of that formula (min/median/max gap, metallic fraction, number of polymorphs). The entry is therefore 'DFT, structure-derived, matched by formula', and the DFT gap / metal flag are close proxies of the matbench_expt_gap and matbench_expt_is_metal targets. No experimental external labels are used: the only experimental labels seen are the task's own training-fold labels. Features: matminer/pymatgen composition descriptors (Magpie and other ElementProperty presets, element fractions, Stoichiometry, ValenceOrbital, IonProperty, BandCenter, AtomicOrbitals, Meredig, Miedema, YangSolidSolution, AtomicPackingEfficiency, WenAlloys, TMetalFraction) and CBFV Oliynyk statistics; all are label-free functions of the formula. Experts: Optuna-tuned LightGBM, XGBoost, CatBoost, extra trees (two feature sets and element fractions), kernel ridge (regression) or RBF SVM (classification), k-nearest neighbours and an MLP; for matbench_expt_gap additionally hurdle experts for the zero-inflated band gap (a classifier for gap > 0 combined with a regressor fitted on the non-zero gaps). Protocol: nested cross-validation inside each official training fold. Five inner folds produce out-of-fold predictions for every expert; hyperparameters, the non-negative stack weights (summing to one; L1 loss for regression, Brier score for classification) and an optional novelty-damped local out-of-fold residual correction are all chosen on these inner folds, and the correction is kept only if a further nested inner-CV check confirms it (it was kept in 0 of 20 task-folds). FOLD USE, STATED EXACTLY. Every choice is made inside the training rows T_k of each official fold k; the test rows are only predicted and recorded. Fold-internal: the Optuna hyperparameters, the simplex stack weights, the correction gate, the classification thresholds, AND the design choices that an earlier version of this entry had fixed from a design phase on fold 0's training rows: the feature-block set (candidates F_min = Magpie + element fractions + extra descriptors; F_red = F_min + DFT block; F_full = F_red + the remaining descriptor blocks) and, for matbench_expt_gap, the use of the hurdle experts and of the element-fraction extra-trees expert. These are now a small candidate set and the choice among the candidates is made per fold by the cross-fitted inner-CV score of the uncorrected stack on T_k (ties to the simpler candidate); for steels and glass the DFT block is empty or nearly empty, so only F_red vs F_full are candidates (matbench_steels: 2 candidates; matbench_expt_gap: 12 candidates; matbench_expt_is_metal: 3 candidates; matbench_glass: 2 candidates). Selected per fold: matbench_steels: fold 0 F_red|hurdle=off|et_frac=in, fold 1 F_red|hurdle=off|et_frac=in, fold 2 F_red|hurdle=off|et_frac=in, fold 3 F_red|hurdle=off|et_frac=in, fold 4 F_red|hurdle=off|et_frac=in; matbench_expt_gap: fold 0 F_full|hurdle=on|et_frac=in, fold 1 F_full|hurdle=on|et_frac=in, fold 2 F_full|hurdle=on|et_frac=out, fold 3 F_full|hurdle=on|et_frac=in, fold 4 F_full|hurdle=on|et_frac=in; matbench_expt_is_metal: fold 0 F_full|hurdle=off|et_frac=in, fold 1 F_full|hurdle=off|et_frac=in, fold 2 F_full|hurdle=off|et_frac=in, fold 3 F_full|hurdle=off|et_frac=in, fold 4 F_full|hurdle=off|et_frac=in; matbench_glass: fold 0 F_full|hurdle=off|et_frac=in, fold 1 F_full|hurdle=off|et_frac=in, fold 2 F_full|hurdle=off|et_frac=in, fold 3 F_full|hurdle=off|et_frac=in, fold 4 F_full|hurdle=off|et_frac=in. NOT fold-internal, disclosed: the candidate set itself was constructed from the alternatives explored on fold 0's training rows, as were the Optuna budget of 20 trials; the dropped experts (random forest, CrabNet, MODNet); restricting CatBoost to the F1 feature set; the fixed SVC C and gamma; and the composition of the candidate set itself; and the label-free imputation described in the notes. The code was frozen (SHA-256 hashes) before the official test folds were predicted with it, and the test folds were predicted and scored once with this configuration. Classification: hard labels are recorded at a decision threshold that maximises balanced accuracy on the training-fold out-of-fold predictions (inner-CV threshold), so the board's ROC-AUC for these tasks equals balanced accuracy.
notes: CPU-only (no GPU). Candidate scoring, selection and final predictions ran on one Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-14650HX workstation (16 cores / 24 threads; 5 parallel workers x 4 threads). The new expert cross-fits of the smaller feature-block candidates ran on the same workstation (steels, glass) and on two cloud CPU pods (AMD EPYC 9575F 64-Core Processor; 32 vCPU each, 8 workers x 4 threads) for expt_gap and expt_is_metal. Expert cross-fits of the earlier run (F_full block set) were reused where the expert reads exactly the same columns (identical computation: same code, seeds, deterministic boosting). Total wall time of the Amendment-3 jobs: 2.2 h over all 20 task-folds (mean per fold: matbench_steels 1 min, matbench_expt_gap 14 min, matbench_expt_is_metal 7 min, matbench_glass 5 min), on top of the 14.3 worker-hours of the reused F_full expert fits. Per-fold compute is recorded in the parameters of every fold in results.json.gz (wall_time_s, n_workers, threads_per_worker, cpu_threads_used, cpu_model, gpu, fit_hosts, expert_fit_seconds per expert, selected_candidate, candidate_inner_cv_scores). DETERMINISM CHECK: fold 0 of matbench_steels and of matbench_expt_gap were re-fitted from scratch on a Linux cloud CPU (AMD EPYC 9575F 64-Core Processor) with the same pinned package versions and compared with the Windows-workstation run (per-expert max |difference| of the test predictions): matbench_expt_gap: cat_F1 0.0e+00, et_F1 8.9e-16, et_F2 8.9e-16, hurdle_et_F1_exp 8.9e-16, hurdle_lgbm_F2_exp 1.7e-21, hurdle_lgbm_F2_median 0.0e+00, knn_frac 0.0e+00, krr_frac 3.9e-13, krr_magpie 5.2e-13, lgbm_F2_tuned 0.0e+00, mlp_F1 1.1e-14, xgb_F2 8.8e-01; re-tuned LightGBM parameters identical; matbench_steels: cat_F1 0.0e+00, et_F1 2.3e-13, et_F2 4.5e-13, et_frac 4.5e-13, knn_frac 0.0e+00, krr_frac 5.4e-11, krr_magpie 1.5e-11, lgbm_F2_tuned 7.8e-02, mlp_F1 1.8e-12, xgb_F2 6.6e+01; re-tuned LightGBM parameters different. Same-machine reruns are exactly reproducible (the reused caches and the from-scratch selection agree to 0.0 wherever the same candidate is selected); across CPU architectures XGBoost (tree_method=hist) and, on the small steels task, the Optuna-tuned LightGBM parameters are not bitwise reproducible, while every other expert agrees to 1e-9 or better. DFT-block coverage (compositions matched by reduced formula): matbench_steels: 0/312 (0%); matbench_expt_gap: 3347/4604 (73%); matbench_expt_is_metal: 3613/4921 (73%); matbench_glass: 60/5680 (1%). PRIOR RUNS ON THE OFFICIAL FOLDS (all reported in the manuscript and in the research repository): (1) Amendment 1 (2026-10-18; no DFT block, no hurdle experts, smaller expert pool, fully fold-internal candidate selection): matbench_steels 82.80 MAE; matbench_expt_gap 0.3240 MAE; matbench_expt_is_metal 0.9370 balanced accuracy; matbench_glass 0.8841 balanced accuracy; probability ROC-AUC matbench_expt_is_metal 0.9825, matbench_glass 0.9567. (2) Amendment 2 (2026-10-19; the present expert pool and features with the design choices fixed from fold 0's training rows; this was the entry as first submitted in this PR): matbench_steels 80.10 MAE; matbench_expt_gap 0.2352 MAE; matbench_expt_is_metal 0.9547 balanced accuracy; matbench_glass 0.8937 balanced accuracy; probability ROC-AUC matbench_expt_is_metal 0.9895, matbench_glass 0.9606. (3) The present entry, Amendment 3 (2026-10-24; same pipeline, design choices selected per fold): matbench_steels 80.32 MAE; matbench_expt_gap 0.2352 MAE; matbench_expt_is_metal 0.9547 balanced accuracy; matbench_glass 0.8937 balanced accuracy. Each run was pre-registered and scored once; Amendment 3 replaces the submitted file because it is the rule-compliant run, whatever its numbers. LABELS VARIANT: results.json.gz records hard labels for the two classification tasks (the 'labels' variant). A 'probabilities' variant (same predictions, probabilities recorded) was written at the same scoring moment and is kept in the research repository; recording labels was fixed in the pre-registered protocol before scoring, because the board compares label-based entries by balanced accuracy. For reference, the probability ROC-AUC of the same predictions is matbench_expt_is_metal 0.9895 ± 0.0008, matbench_glass 0.9606 ± 0.0080, and matbench itself would score the probabilities file (thresholded at 0.5) at matbench_expt_is_metal 0.9559, matbench_glass 0.8725. TRANSDUCTIVE BUT LABEL-FREE IMPUTATION: two feature builders fill rare missing descriptor values with column medians computed over all rows of a task (training and test rows together; no labels): CBFV generate_features for the Oliynyk block and the 'extra' matminer block in dftstack/data.py. Cells filled, per task: matbench_steels: CBFV 0 of 96096 cells (0 rows), extra block 0 of 6552 cells (0 rows); matbench_expt_gap: CBFV 2782 of 1418032 cells (422 rows), extra block 42 of 96684 cells (14 rows); matbench_expt_is_metal: CBFV 3075 of 1515668 cells (465 rows), extra block 42 of 103341 cells (14 rows); matbench_glass: CBFV 132 of 1749440 cells (22 rows), extra block 63 of 119280 cells (21 rows). Columns that are entirely missing are dropped on the same basis. matbench==0.6 was installed with --no-deps because its scikit-learn==1.0 / monty pins do not build on Python 3.12; the newer versions listed in requirements were used. The folder is self-contained: run_submission.py plus the dftstack/ package (verbatim copies of the frozen research modules, including the per-fold candidate selection) reproduce results.json.gz and record every fold with task.record; the Matbench tasks and the matminer DFT datasets are downloaded on first use. Full research repository (analysis plan with all amendments, freeze hashes, per-fold predictions, candidate scores, ablations): https://github.com/bhaskargurram-ai/matbench-composition-stack. The matbench 0.6 wheel writes plain JSON even for a .gz filename; the file here is the byte-identical JSON gzip-compressed, which is what MatbenchBenchmark.from_file on the current main branch reads (run_submission.py compresses its output the same way).
